bond-deportation-package.title: Bond + Deportation Defense Package
bond-deportation-package.short: One team. One fee. Start to finish.
bond-deportation-package.headline: Out of custody. Into court. Home safe.
bond-deportation-package.overview1: This package combines the bond fight and the removal defense into a single engagement. You get coordinated strategy, no handoff gaps, and a single written fee covering both phases.
bond-deportation-package.overview2: It's designed for families dealing with a detained loved one who also wants a dedicated defense team for the underlying removal case. Most clients start here when ICE custody is involved.
bond-deportation-package.overview3: We handle bond, transfer monitoring if ICE moves the client, and every stage of the removal case through final hearing and appeal.
bond-deportation-package.step2Desc: Bond granted or custody redetermined; coordinate release logistics.
bond-deportation-package.step3Desc: Identify every form of relief (cancellation, asylum, adjustment, withholding, CAT).
bond-deportation-package.step4Desc: Evidence gathering, mock hearings, witness and expert prep.
bond-deportation-package.step5Desc: Full merits representation, with BIA appeal included if needed.

bond-habeas.title: Bond + Habeas Corpus
bond-habeas.short: When ICE holds you past the law, we go to federal court.
bond-habeas.headline: There is a deadline the government has to follow. We enforce it.
bond-habeas.forms: 28 U.S.C. § 2241 petition, evidence of prolonged detention
bond-habeas.overview1: Some detention is unlawful — mandatory detention that's gone on too long, post-order detention past the Zadvydas six-month mark, or detention without a bond hearing at all. Federal habeas relief can force release.
bond-habeas.overview2: We combine a bond filing (when available) with a federal habeas petition to attack the detention on multiple fronts simultaneously.
bond-habeas.overview3: These are complex cases with short windows. We move fast and we don't take them unless we can build a real record.
bond-habeas.step1Desc: Review custody history, statutory basis, and Zadvydas/Demore posture.
bond-habeas.step2Desc: File a bond motion with the immigration court if a bond hearing is available.
bond-habeas.step3Desc: File a habeas petition in the appropriate U.S. District Court.
bond-habeas.step4Desc: Draft reply brief; oral argument where set.
bond-habeas.step5Desc: Court-ordered release with conditions, or remand for a bond hearing.

bia-appeal.title: BIA Appeal
bia-appeal.short: The judge's decision isn't the last word.
bia-appeal.headline: The fight isn't over. It just moved upstairs.
bia-appeal.overview1: If an immigration judge denies your relief, you have 30 days to file a Notice of Appeal with the BIA. Missing the deadline is fatal. Timing, filing, and framing the legal issues correctly are everything.
bia-appeal.overview2: BIA appeals are won or lost in the legal brief. We identify reversible errors, preserve issues for federal court review, and write briefs that read like federal appellate work.
bia-appeal.overview3: We also take over mid-appeal when an existing brief is underdeveloped or when another attorney missed the deadline.
bia-appeal.step1Desc: Obtain the full administrative record and transcript.
bia-appeal.step2Desc: Identify legal and factual errors preserved for review.
bia-appeal.step3Desc: Full appellate brief with record citations.
bia-appeal.step4Desc: File on time; reply to DHS brief where allowed.
bia-appeal.step5Desc: If remanded: back to IJ. If denied: petition for review at the circuit court.

motion-to-reopen.title: Motion to Reopen
motion-to-reopen.short: New facts deserve a new look.
motion-to-reopen.headline: A closed case isn't always a dead case.
motion-to-reopen.overview1: A motion to reopen asks the court to reconsider a prior decision based on material facts that weren't available before. Common grounds: ineffective assistance of counsel, changed country conditions, new qualifying relative.
motion-to-reopen.overview2: Deadlines and numerical limits apply (generally one motion within 90 days), with statutory exceptions for certain grounds. Filing the right motion on the right schedule is critical.
motion-to-reopen.overview3: We evaluate quickly, gather the supporting evidence, and file a tightly-argued motion with the legal framework the adjudicator needs to grant.
motion-to-reopen.step1Desc: Assess the legal ground and whether a time/number exception applies.
motion-to-reopen.step2Desc: Affidavits, new evidence, country reports, expert reports if applicable.
motion-to-reopen.step3Desc: Fact and law sections with careful record citations.
motion-to-reopen.step4Desc: File with court or BIA; reply to DHS opposition.
motion-to-reopen.step5Desc: Reopening granted: back to hearing. Denied: federal review options.

motion-to-terminate.title: Motion to Terminate
motion-to-terminate.short: Sometimes the best defense is no case at all.
motion-to-terminate.headline: End the proceedings before they can end you.
motion-to-terminate.overview1: Termination ends the removal case. Grounds include defective Notices to Appear (Niz-Chavez issues), prosecutorial discretion, or pending USCIS relief that makes continued proceedings inappropriate.
motion-to-terminate.overview2: DHS can oppose or join. We prepare the motion, coordinate with the OPLA prosecutor, and push for termination or administrative closure where termination is unavailable.
motion-to-terminate.overview3: For clients with strong equities and no removability issue, termination is often a cleaner path than fighting for relief in court.
motion-to-terminate.step1Desc: Assess the NTA for defects and check eligibility for USCIS relief.
motion-to-terminate.step3Desc: File the motion with supporting brief and evidence.
motion-to-terminate.step4Desc: Oral argument if the court sets one.
motion-to-terminate.step5Desc: Termination, administrative closure, or denial — next steps prepared for each.

change-of-venue.title: Change of Venue
change-of-venue.short: You shouldn't have to cross three states for a hearing.
change-of-venue.headline: The right court. Closer to you.
change-of-venue.forms: Motion to change venue, address evidence
change-of-venue.overview1: If you've moved since your case was filed, a change of venue motion moves your case to the court that serves your new address. Getting venue right matters: judge patterns, scheduling, and logistics all change by court.
change-of-venue.overview2: This is usually an add-on service combined with a full engagement, but can be a standalone filing where the client already has counsel handling the merits.
change-of-venue.overview3: We handle notification to ICE OPLA, address evidence, and follow-up confirmation that the transfer actually completed.
change-of-venue.step1Desc: Collect lease, utility bills, and other address proof.
change-of-venue.step2Desc: Draft the motion with legal basis and good cause.
change-of-venue.step3Desc: File with the current court and serve on OPLA.
change-of-venue.step4Desc: Confirm the case actually moves to the new court.
change-of-venue.step5Desc: Confirm new Master Calendar date and prepare accordingly.

circuit-appeal.title: Petition for Review (Circuit Court)
circuit-appeal.short: Federal court is the last honest look your case gets.
circuit-appeal.headline: When the agency won't budge, the circuit can.
circuit-appeal.forms: Petition for review, appellate brief, record
circuit-appeal.overview1: If the BIA affirms a denial, you have 30 days to file a petition for review in the federal circuit court covering where the immigration judge sat. Federal judges review for legal and constitutional errors.
circuit-appeal.overview2: These cases require federal appellate skill — record citations, legal framing, and argument in open court before a three-judge panel. We brief them like the federal appeals they are.
circuit-appeal.overview3: Rafael is admitted to the Eleventh Circuit. For cases in other circuits we associate with admitted local counsel.
circuit-appeal.step1Desc: Obtain and read the entire administrative record.
circuit-appeal.step2Desc: Legal errors, due process, constitutional issues.
circuit-appeal.step3Desc: Fully briefed with standards of review, argument, and conclusion.
circuit-appeal.step4Desc: If the court grants argument, prep and present.
circuit-appeal.step5Desc: If remanded: back to BIA/IJ. Further review via Supreme Court rare but considered.

habeas-corpus.title: Habeas Corpus
habeas-corpus.short: Unlawful detention has a federal remedy.
habeas-corpus.headline: The Constitution doesn't pause at the detention center door.
habeas-corpus.forms: 28 U.S.C. § 2241 petition, evidence of prolonged detention
habeas-corpus.overview1: Federal habeas under 28 U.S.C. § 2241 can challenge the legality of ICE detention when removal is not reasonably foreseeable (Zadvydas), when mandatory detention is prolonged (Demore/Jennings), or when a bond hearing was improperly denied.
habeas-corpus.overview2: Habeas petitions are filed in the U.S. District Court where the detainee is held. We draft the petition, coordinate service on the government, and argue the motion to release.
habeas-corpus.overview3: Not every prolonged detention qualifies. We evaluate realistically and only take cases where there's a viable legal theory.
habeas-corpus.step1Desc: Review custody history and statutory basis.
habeas-corpus.step2Desc: Draft habeas petition with declarations and exhibits.
habeas-corpus.step3Desc: File in the appropriate district court; serve DHS/ICE.
habeas-corpus.step4Desc: Review government brief; file reply and any amended petition.
habeas-corpus.step5Desc: Court-ordered release, bond hearing, or denial — appeal ready if needed.

family-petitions.title: Family-Based Petitions (I-130)
family-petitions.short: The paperwork that keeps families under one roof.
family-petitions.headline: Reuniting families — one petition at a time.
family-petitions.timeline: Immediate relatives: 8–16 months. Preference categories: variable.
family-petitions.overview1: The I-130 is the foundation of most family immigration cases. It establishes a qualifying relationship between a U.S. citizen or LPR petitioner and a foreign national beneficiary.
family-petitions.overview2: Our I-130 work focuses on proving bona fides decisively: joint financial records, photographs over time, affidavits from people who know both spouses, travel records, and evidence of shared life.
family-petitions.overview3: Adjustment of status (I-485) is a separate engagement, but we frequently bundle them for clients already in the U.S.
family-petitions.step1Desc: Gather certificates, photos, joint accounts, affidavits, proof of cohabitation.
family-petitions.step2Desc: Complete the form with careful accuracy.
family-petitions.step3Desc: File with USCIS with all supporting evidence.
family-petitions.step4Desc: Respond promptly to Requests for Evidence if USCIS issues one.
family-petitions.step5Desc: Receive I-130 approval; proceed to I-485 adjustment or consular processing.
